subject: Tiered credit escrow and price-floor discussion
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@elaralabs.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tiered credit escrow and price-floor discussion

Hi Sara —

Great to chat earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on numbers and what I’ll put in the formal proposal:

Call highlights
- Primary use case: RAG + high-QA assistant for product discovery flows.
- Near-term expected consumption (month 0–3): 5M–25M tokens / month.
- Target ramp: ~100M tokens / month by month 12 assuming successful pilot.
- Budget signal you gave on call: $15k–$40k / month initially; want unit economics in the $/1M tokens band to map to that range.

You asked for three things I’ll include in the proposal:
1) Startup program credits applied to first 3 months (we usually do a tiered credit up to a cap).
2) Committed-use discount scenarios for 6/12/24 month prepay with corresponding unit rates and a price floor.
3) An escrow or prepaid drawdown option to keep billing predictable for procurement.

Initial pricing mechanics (to validate):
- On-demand baseline: $150 / 1M tokens (for reference only).
- Startup package: 50% credit for months 1–3 up to $25k total credit (needs qualification).
- Committed tiers: 6mo = 10% off baseline, 12mo = 20% off, 24mo = 30% off.
- Example: a 12mo committed prepay of $600k maps to an effective ~$95 / 1M tokens for the committed bucket (depends on usage mix).
- We can add a price floor mechanic: reserved bucket rate applies down to X $/1M; usage above reserved is metered.

Escrow idea (ops-friendly option)
- Customer prepays into an escrow account; monthly drawdown against usage; unspent funds returned at end of term or converted to credits.
- This helps procurement avoid invoice volatility while giving you predictable unit economics.

Attachments I’ll include in the formal send: redwood-commit-scenarios-v2.xlsx (breaks down math and example banding).

Next steps
- I’ll send a formal proposal with 3 scenarios (startup + 6mo + 12mo) by EOD tomorrow.
- Can you confirm the budget cadence procurement needs (monthly vs quarterly invoicing), and whether Ben Lee (procurement) should be on the signature/negotiation thread?

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa (finance) if we need invoice/PO language.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
From: Sara Patel <sara@elaralabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Lee <ben@elaralabs.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Tiered credit escrow and price-floor discussion

Jordan —

Thanks for the recap — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side after reviewing the internal budget:

Token profile
- Pilot (M0–M3): plan for 10M tokens / month average (conservative).
- Scale target: 80–120M tokens / month by month 9–12 depending on feature rollout.

Budget & pricing constraints
- Finance is comfortable with ~$20k–$35k / month for the first 3–6 months; beyond that we can revisit.
- Our procurement requirement: minimum committed floor is preferred, but we need a clear mechanism to avoid being locked into overcommit if the product changes.

Specific asks
1) Can you include a 12-month committed example that hits an effective $/1M tokens of $85–$105 depending on volume bands?
2) Can the startup credit be structured so it doesn’t count against the committed bucket (i.e., credits applied on top of the committed allowance)?
3) We prefer the escrow drawdown approach — can you provide language for how unused escrow balances are returned?
4) We need SOC 2 Type II and a simple SOW + DocuSign flow for legal.

I’ve looped Ben (procurement) for timelines — Ben, can you share the standard PO review SLA?

If you can get the proposal and the DocuSign link this week, I’ll route to procurement and legal.

—Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product, Elara Labs
sara@elaralabs.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@elaralabs.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered credit escrow and price-floor discussion

Sara —

Thanks — noted. I’ve updated the scenarios and attached a clean pricing workbook and a short procurement checklist (procurement-checklist.pdf) to this thread. High level answers below; full numbers are in the spreadsheet.

Committed scenarios (summary)
- 6mo committed (prepay): effective 12% off baseline, example: $420k prepay -> ~$105 / 1M tokens for committed bucket.
- 12mo committed (prepay): effective 20% off baseline -> example: $600k prepay -> ~$95 / 1M tokens.
- 24mo committed (prepay): effective 30% off baseline -> example: $1.2M prepay -> ~$75–$85 / 1M tokens depending on staircase bands.

On your asks:
1) 12-month example: I can structure a multiband that gives you $85–$105 / 1M depending on monthly consumption bands — spreadsheet shows the thresholds.
2) Startup credits: yes — they can be additive to the committed allowance for the initial period. We’ll mark credits as promotional line items in the invoice.
3) Escrow mechanics: Redwood will accept prepay to a restricted account; monthly usage is debited. Unused escrow at term-end can either be refunded or converted to additional credits at your election. I’ll include precise contract language in the proposal.
4) SOC 2 Type II: attaching the secure portal link and we’ll include the cert in the contract package. Legal will push a short SOW + DocuSign envelope.

Procurement notes (for Ben)
- We can support monthly invoicing against escrow or a single prepay invoice.
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 after invoice; we can discuss Net 45 for larger prepay.
- Required docs we typically need for POs: W-9, signed SOW, billing contact, and PO number.

I’ve attached: redwood-commit-scenarios-v2.xlsx and procurement-checklist.pdf. I’ll send a DocuSign envelope with the proposal (and the SOW) tomorrow morning for your review.

Let me know if there’s any change to the budget cadence. If you approve the 12mo scenario I’ll ask Marissa to prepare a formal quote.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake

Thanks for being flexible on the startup credit stacking. Once we have the DocuSign link I’ll route it to legal and procurement.

—Sara
